data_source_url.description: Optionally restrict semantic search to a data source URL returned in a <data-source> tag.

max_highlight_length.description: Maximum result highlight length (default 200). Set to 0 to omit highlights.

page_size.description: Maximum number of results to return (default 10).

page_url.description: Optionally restrict semantic search to a page and its descendants. Accepts a Notion page URL or ID.

query.description: A concise natural-language semantic search query, ideally under 50 words.

teamspace_id.description: Optionally restrict semantic search to a teamspace ID.

page_url.description: The full Notion URL of the page to mark as a skill.

content.description: The complete UTF-8 text content of the file. Maximum 200 KiB after UTF-8 encoding. Requires filename.

content_type.description: Optional MIME type, such as text/html or application/pdf. It must match the filename extension; omit it to infer the type from the filename. Omit it with source_file_id; the stored upload already carries a content type.

filename.description: The filename to create in Notion, including a supported extension such as .html, .md, .pdf, or .png. Required with content and source_url. Omit it with source_file_id; the stored upload already carries a filename.

source_file_id.description: The ID of a file upload this exact integration already created, using create_file_upload when available or the Notion File Upload API with this integration's token. Its status must be uploaded.

source_url.description: A direct, publicly reachable HTTPS URL from which Notion can download the file within one minute. Redirects, private network addresses, custom request headers, and cookies are not supported. Requires filename.

discussion_id.description: The ID or URL of an existing discussion to reply to (e.g., discussion://pageId/blockId/discussionId).

markdown.description: The content of the comment as a Markdown string. Provide exactly one of markdown or rich_text. For exact syntax, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/enhanced-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Use only the Rich text types and Mentions syntax that comments support. Comments support inline formatting (bold, italic, strikethrough, underline, code, links), inline math using $`Equation`$, and user/page/database/date mention tags such as <mention-date start="YYYY-MM-DD"/>. To attach a file created by create-file-upload or create-attachment, include its returned suggested_markdown on a separate line; up to three file attachments are supported. Do not use UI shortcuts like @today, @name, [[page]], or autocomplete-style emoji syntax; those are editor affordances, not markdown syntax. Mention tags must include a real url where required by the spec. Other block-level Markdown such as fenced code blocks, headings, lists, tables, and blockquotes is stored as plain comment text rather than rendered as blocks.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to comment on (with or without dashes).

rich_text.description: An array of rich text objects that represent the content of the comment. Provide exactly one of rich_text or markdown.

annotations.description: All rich text objects contain an annotations object that sets the styling for the rich text.

bold.description: Whether the text is formatted as bold.

code.description: Whether the text is formatted as code.

italic.description: Whether the text is formatted as italic.

strikethrough.description: Whether the text is formatted with a strikethrough.

underline.description: Whether the text is formatted with an underline.

text.description: If a rich text object's type value is `text`, then the corresponding text field contains an object including the text content and any inline link.

content.description: The actual text content of the text.

link.description: An object with information about any inline link in this text, if included.

end.description: The end date of the date object, if any.

start.description: The start date of the date object.

time_zone.description: The time zone of the date object, if any. E.g. America/Los_Angeles, Europe/London, etc.

id.description: The ID of the page in the mention.
The ID of the database in the mention.

template_mention_date.description: The date of the template mention.

custom_emoji.description: Details of the custom emoji mention.

id.description: The ID of the custom emoji.

name.description: The name of the custom emoji.

url.description: The URL of the custom emoji.

mention.description: Mention objects represent an inline mention of a database, date, link preview mention, page, template mention, or user. A mention is created in the Notion UI when a user types `@` followed by the name of the reference.

equation.description: Notion supports inline LaTeX equations as rich text objects with a type value of `equation`.

selection_with_ellipsis.description: Unique start and end snippet of the content to comment on. DO NOT provide the entire string. Instead, provide up to the first ~10 characters, an ellipsis, and then up to the last ~10 characters. Make sure you provide enough of the start and end snippet to uniquely identify the content. For example: "# Section heading...last paragraph."

database_type.description: Create a canonical typed database with Notion's required properties and metadata. Supported types: tasks, projects, skills.

description.description: The description of the new database.

parent.description: The parent under which to create the new database. If omitted, the database will be created as a private page at the workspace level.

page_id.description: The ID of the parent page, with or without dashes.

schema.description: SQL DDL CREATE TABLE statement defining the database schema. Cannot be combined with database_type. Column names must be double-quoted and type options use single quotes.

title.description: The title of the new database.

content_type.description: Optional MIME type, such as application/pdf or image/png. Prefer omitting it so the type is inferred from the filename: a type that disagrees with the extension is stored as given, and the file then renders as the wrong kind.

filename.description: The filename to create in Notion, including a supported extension such as .pdf, .png, or .zip.

page_id.description: The ID of the page that will own the Folder.

folder_id.description: The ID of the Folder that will contain the new Folder.

title.description: The title of the new Folder.

allow_async.description: Default to true for page creation. Set to false only when the next step needs the created pages immediately, or when async execution rejects the request as too large. When this create operation is accepted for background execution, it returns an async_task result. Use get_async_task to wait for a succeeded status before taking a dependent action on the pages. For pages created with template_id, a succeeded status does not mean template content is ready; fetch and retry until it is ready before changing or relying on that content. If omitted or false, the tool keeps the existing synchronous result shape.

content.description: The content of the new page, using Notion Markdown.

cover.description: An external image URL for the page cover. Use "none" to explicitly set no cover. Omit to leave unchanged.

icon.description: An emoji character (e.g. "🚀"), a custom emoji by name (e.g. ":rocket_ship:"), or an external image URL. Use "none" to explicitly set no icon. Omit to leave unchanged.

is_skill.description: Set to true to create this page as a reusable skill. Before using this field, read the "notion://docs/skills" resource for authoring guidance. False has the same effect as omitting the field.

preserve_internal_links.description: Preserve internal Markdown links instead of converting them to native mentions.

properties.description: The properties of the new page, which is a JSON map of property names to SQLite values. For pages in a database, use the SQLite schema definition shown in <database>. For pages outside of a database, the only allowed property is "title", which is the title of the page and is automatically shown at the top of the page as a large heading.

template_id.description: The ID of a template to apply to this page. When specified, do not provide 'content' as the template will provide it. Properties can still be set alongside the template. Get template IDs from the <templates> section in the fetch tool results.

page_id.description: The ID of the parent page (with or without dashes), for example, 195de9221179449fab8075a27c979105

database_id.description: The ID of the parent database (with or without dashes), for example, 195de9221179449fab8075a27c979105

data_source_id.description: The ID of the parent data source (collection), with or without dashes. For example, f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd

parent.description: The parent under which the new pages will be created. This can be a page (page_id), a database page (database_id), or a data source/collection under a database (data_source_id). If the user names a private or shared destination, use it as the parent. If omitted, the new pages will be created as private pages at the workspace level. When no destination is named, prefer explicit "creation_mode": "draft" instead of simply omitting the parent. Use data_source_id when you have a collection:// URL from the fetch tool.

configure.description: View configuration DSL string. Supports FILTER, SORT BY, GROUP BY, CALENDAR BY, TIMELINE BY, MAP BY, CHART, FORM, SHOW, HIDE, COVER, WRAP CELLS, and FREEZE COLUMNS directives. See notion://docs/view-dsl-spec.

data_source_id.description: The data source (collection) ID. Accepts a collection:// URI from <data-source> tags or a bare UUID.

database_id.description: The database to add a view tab to. Accepts a Notion URL or a bare UUID. Mutually exclusive with `parent_page_id`; exactly one must be provided.

parent_page_id.description: A page to create an inline linked database view on. Accepts a Notion URL or a bare UUID. The new linked view block is appended at the end of the page and references `data_source_id`. Mutually exclusive with `database_id`; exactly one must be provided.

type.description: The type of view to create.

file_upload_id.description: The FileUpload ID returned by the create-attachment tool.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to duplicate. This is a v4 UUID, with or without dashes, and can be parsed from a Notion page URL.

id.description: The ID or URL of the Notion page, database, or data source to fetch. Supports notion.so URLs, Notion Sites URLs (*.notion.site), raw UUIDs, and data source URLs (collection://...). Pass "self" to fetch the connected workspace and user identity. Pass a notion://docs/* URI to read that documentation resource.

include_discussions.description: Whether to include discussion/comment indicators in the page output. When true, adds a <page-discussions> summary with discussion count, preview snippets, and discussion:// URLs. Use with the get_comments tool to retrieve full discussion content. Defaults to false.

include_transcript.description: Whether to include meeting note transcripts. Defaults to false. When true, full transcripts are included; when false, a placeholder with the meeting note URL is shown instead.

task_id.description: The ID of the async task to retrieve, as returned in the async_task response of the tool that started it.

discussion_id.description: Fetch a specific discussion by ID or discussion URL (e.g., discussion://pageId/blockId/discussionId).

include_all_blocks.description: Include discussions on child blocks, not just page-level discussions. Defaults to false.

include_resolved.description: Include resolved discussions in the response. Defaults to false.

query.description: Optional search query to filter teams by name (case-insensitive).

page_size.description: Number of users to return per page (1–100; default 100).

query.description: Optional search query to filter users by name or email (case-insensitive).

start_cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the next_cursor value from the previous response to get the next page.

user_id.description: Return only the user matching this ID. Pass "self" to fetch the current user.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from the previous response.
Opaque pagination cursor from the previous response.
Opaque pagination cursor from the previous response.

after_sequence.description: Load the next page of events starting after this sequence number.

before_sequence.description: Load the previous page of events ending before this sequence number.

count.description: Maximum number of committed events to return.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from the previous response.

page_id.description: The ID of the parent page (with or without dashes), for example, 195de9221179449fab8075a27c979105

database_id.description: The ID of the parent database (with or without dashes), for example, 195de9221179449fab8075a27c979105

data_source_id.description: The ID of the parent data source (collection), with or without dashes. For example, f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd

new_parent.description: The new parent under which the pages will be moved. This can be a page, the workspace, a database, or a specific data source under a database when there are multiple. Moving pages to the workspace level adds them as private pages and should rarely be used.

page_or_database_ids.description: An array of up to 100 page or database IDs to move. IDs are v4 UUIDs and can be supplied with or without dashes (e.g. extracted from a <page> or <database> URL given by the "search" or "fetch" tool). Data Sources under Databases can't be moved individually.

data_source_urls.description: Notion data source URLs whose SQLite tables are available to the query; each data source is exposed as a table named by its URL. Obtain them from the fetch tool, in the format: collection://f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd

params.description: Positional parameters bound to `?` placeholders in the query. Prefer parameterized queries over string interpolation. Use "__YES__" for checked checkboxes and "__NO__" for unchecked checkboxes.

query.description: Read-only SQLite query to execute against the data sources. Use a data source URL as the table name, e.g. SELECT * FROM "collection://..." WHERE .... Include every needed filter in WHERE (filters on views of the data source are not automatically applied). For time comparisons or ordering, normalize text timestamps with datetime(...) or date(...). SQL text values can omit rich-text mentions and formatting, and links can lose their destination. Use faithful rows mode or fetch the page before rewriting a rich-text property.

is_archived.description: Optional archive selector. Omitted or false queries non-archived rows only; true queries archived rows only.

page_size.description: Number of rows to return per page (default: 100, max: 100).

start_cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the next_cursor value from the previous response to get the next page.

view_url.description: URL of a specific database view to query. Example: https://www.notion.so/workspace/db-id?v=view-id

data_source_url.description: One Notion data source URL obtained from a fetch result.

filter.description: A session property filter, or an and/or compound filter nested up to two levels deep.

page_size.description: The number of sessions to return. Maximum: 100.

query.description: A case-insensitive substring search over session titles.

sorts.description: Ordered sort precedence. Defaults to updated_at descending.

property.description: One of: `created_at`, `updated_at`

start_cursor.description: The continuation cursor returned by the previous page.

sequence.description: Committed event sequence number to read.

data_source_url.description: Optionally restrict keyword search to a data source URL returned in a <data-source> tag.

filters.description: Optionally provide exact filters for Notion workspace search.

content_status.description: Which pages to include by status. Defaults to live pages only. Available on the Business plan.

created_by_user_ids.description: Optional filter to only produce search results created by the Notion users that have the specified user IDs.

created_date_range.description: Optional filter to only produce search results created within the specified date range.

end_date.description: The end date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

start_date.description: The start date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

edited_by_user_ids.description: Optional filter to only produce search results edited by the Notion users that have the specified user IDs. Available on the Business plan.

last_edited_date_range.description: Optional filter to only produce search results last edited within the specified date range. Available on the Business plan.

end_date.description: The end date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

start_date.description: The start date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

teamspace_ids.description: Optional filter to only produce search results inside one of the specified teamspaces. Selecting more than one teamspace is available on the Business plan; use teamspace_id for one teamspace on other plans.

title_only.description: When true, match the query only against page and database titles instead of page content. Available on the Business plan.

max_highlight_length.description: Maximum character length for result highlights (default 200). Set to 0 to omit highlights entirely.

page_size.description: Maximum number of results to return (default 10). Lower values reduce response size.

page_url.description: Optionally restrict keyword search to a page and its descendants. Accepts a Notion page URL or ID.

query.description: Short, specific keywords for exact matching in Notion. This is not semantic search. For user search, enter a name or email address. An empty query is allowed with filters or a non-relevance sort.

query_type.description: Specify type of the query as either "internal" or "user". Always include this input if performing "user" search.

sort.description: Result ordering for Notion workspace search. Defaults to "relevance".

teamspace_id.description: Optionally, provide the ID of a teamspace to restrict search results to. This will perform a search over content within the specified teamspace only. Accepts the teamspace ID (UUIDv4) with or without dashes.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from the previous response.

query.description: Search text matched against agent names and descriptions. Queries return one page and cannot use a cursor. When omitted, favorites are returned in sidebar order and workspace agents are returned newest first.

scope.description: Which agents to list: "favorites" for the current user's favorite agents, or "workspace" for agents shared with the workspace.

lookback.description: How far back to search, such as "30d" or "1y". Leave it out to search the past year.

question.description: What you want to find in past sessions.

query.description: A Skill name or a short description of the task. Omit to list up to 10 recent Skills.

agent_url.description: Published Custom Agent URL in agent://<spaceId>/<agentId> format, as returned by search_agents.

initial_message.description: Initial message for the new session.

data_source_id.description: The data source to update. Accepts a collection:// URI from <data-source> tags, a bare UUID, or a database ID (only if the database has a single data source).

description.description: The new description of the data source.

in_trash.description: Move data source to trash. Cannot be undone without Notion UI.

is_inline.description: Whether the database should display inline (true) or as full page (false). Only applicable for single-source databases.

statements.description: Semicolon-separated SQL DDL statements to update the schema. Supports ADD COLUMN, DROP COLUMN, RENAME COLUMN, ALTER COLUMN SET.

title.description: The new title of the data source.

file_upload_ids.description: Required for add_files. One or more file upload IDs returned by the file upload tools.

file_urls.description: Required for remove_files. The exact file URLs shown in the Folder's latest fetch output.

folder_id.description: The ID of the Folder to update.

title.description: Required for add_subfolder. The new Folder's title.

allow_async.description: Default to true for page updates. Set to false only when the next step needs the updated page immediately, or when async execution rejects the request as too large. When this update operation is accepted for background execution, it returns an async_task result. Use get_async_task to wait for a succeeded status before taking a dependent action on the page. For apply_template, a succeeded status does not mean template content is ready; fetch and retry until it is ready before changing or relying on that content. If omitted or false, the tool waits for a synchronous result when possible, but may still return a pollable async_task response if queued execution exceeds the synchronous wait deadline.

allow_deleting_content.description: Optional for "replace_content" and "update_content" commands. Set to true to allow deletion of child pages and databases that are not referenced in the new content. If false or omitted, the operation will fail with an error listing the pages/databases that would be deleted.

content.description: Required for "insert_content" command. The markdown content to insert into the page.

content_updates.description: Required for "update_content" command. An array of search-and-replace operations, each with old_str (content to find) and new_str (replacement content).

new_str.description: The new content string to replace old_str with.

old_str.description: The existing content string to find and replace. Must exactly match the page content.

replace_all_matches.description: If true, replaces all occurrences of old_str. If false (default), the operation fails if there are multiple matches.

cover.description: An external image URL for the page cover. Use "none" to remove the cover. Omit to leave unchanged. Can be set alongside any command.

icon.description: An emoji character (e.g. "🚀"), a custom emoji by name (e.g. ":rocket_ship:"), or an external image URL. Use "none" to remove the icon. Omit to leave unchanged. Can be set alongside any command.

is_skill.description: Set to true to mark this page as a skill, or false to remove the skill designation. Can be set alongside any command.

new_str.description: Required for "replace_content" command. The new content string to replace the entire page content with.

page_id.description: The ID of the page to update, with or without dashes.

position.description: Optional for "insert_content" command. Use {"type":"start"} to prepend content or {"type":"end"} to append content. Omit to append.

file_upload.description: The uploaded file to attach to the Files property.

id.description: ID of a file upload returned by create_file_upload or create_attachment.

properties.description: Required for "update_properties" command. A JSON object that updates the page's properties. For pages in a database, use the SQLite schema definition shown in <database>. For pages outside of a database, the only allowed property is "title", which is the title of the page in inline markdown format. For a Files property, an uploaded file can be provided as {"type":"file_upload","file_upload":{"id":"<file-upload-id>"}} inside the property's array. Use null to remove a property's value.

template_id.description: Required for "apply_template" command. The ID of a template to apply to this page. Template content is appended to any existing page content.

verification_expiry_days.description: Optional for "update_verification" command when verification_status is "verified". Number of days until verification expires (e.g. 7, 30, 90). Omit for indefinite verification.

verification_status.description: Required for "update_verification" command. Set to "verified" to mark the page as verified, or "unverified" to remove verification. When updating verification, the owner will be automatically set to the authenticated actor.

configure.description: View configuration DSL string. Supports FILTER, SORT BY, GROUP BY, CALENDAR BY, TIMELINE BY, MAP BY, CHART, FORM, SHOW, HIDE, COVER, WRAP CELLS, FREEZE COLUMNS, and CLEAR directives.

view_id.description: The view to update. Accepts a view:// URI, a Notion URL with ?v= parameter, or a bare UUID.

seconds.description: Maximum number of seconds to wait.
